skill.name: security-audit
skill.description: Use squirrelscan to review website security and integrity findings, including exposed credentials, weak headers, and signs of compromise. Identify skipped checks and prioritize fixes.
skill.summary: Turn website security findings into a prioritized remediation plan.
skill.author: squirrelscan
skill.license: See LICENSE file in repository root

security_audit.summary: The documented installer executes remote code without verification, and the skill instructs agents to run network probes that can affect a target. The report export starts a new audit without preserving the chosen probe or publication settings. Most other matches are Markdown references or reporting guidance, and no evidence of an attempt to override the marketplace review was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the remote shell pipeline with a versioned release and require signature or checksum verification. Ask for explicit approval before installing anything.

remediation.issue: Report export does not inherit audit restrictions
remediation.suggestion: Export from the existing audit without recrawling. Keep target, probe, and publication settings fixed across retries. Report checks outside the approved scope as not checked.

remediation.issue: Network probes can change target state
remediation.suggestion: Default to passive checks and remove state-changing probes from agent workflows. Require separate approval for any active check and enforce target and request limits.

remediation.issue: Full audit exports can include sensitive evidence
remediation.suggestion: Redact sensitive values before export. Ask where to store the report and restrict access to that location.

content.value_statement: Website audit results can hide urgent issues among routine warnings and skipped checks. Use squirrelscan findings to prioritize fixes, document coverage gaps, and plan follow-up.
actual_capabilities: Reviews security and integrity results from the squirrelscan CLI or hosted MCP server.
Identifies checks that were skipped and reports them separately from checks that passed.
Prioritizes suspected compromise and exposed credentials ahead of routine header and cookie fixes.
Recommends credential rotation and describes findings without repeating secret values.
Points to relevant configuration areas for platforms such as Next.js, WordPress, and Vercel.
Uses existing audit IDs to render a filtered CLI report without recrawling.
limitations: This is not a penetration test. A report without findings does not prove a site is secure.
Fresh results require an installed squirrelscan CLI or a connected hosted MCP server.
Passive audits still crawl pages and skip checks that require active probes.
Signed-in audits can use credits and publish unlisted reports. Some fixes also require access to the hosting or credential provider.

use_cases.title: Sort Findings Before a Release
use_cases.description: Review an existing staging report. Separate HTTPS, header, and cookie fixes from checks that did not run.

use_cases.title: Triage Suspected Credential Exposure
use_cases.description: Use a redacted audit report to identify which credentials need rotation and which findings need incident response.

use_cases.title: Review Coverage After Fixes
use_cases.description: Compare existing reports to see which findings changed and which checks still lack evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize this website audit report in plain language. List skipped checks separately and use only the report I provided.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Configuration Fixes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Plan changes for a Next.js site
prompt_templates.prompt: Group the HTTPS, header, and cookie findings from this staging report by priority. Suggest where to review the configuration without editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Incident Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this redacted report for signs of compromise or credential exposure. List evidence, rotation tasks, and open questions without repeating any credential values.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Audit Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Verify fixes using two existing reports
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these audit reports for the same site. Separate resolved findings from skipped checks and document any changes in coverage. Do not run another audit.

output_examples.input: Summarize the transport findings and skipped checks from this staging report.
output: Mixed content: One page loads an image over HTTP. Update the image URL to HTTPS and verify the page.
Coverage gap: Exposure checks were skipped. This report cannot establish whether sensitive files or endpoints are exposed.

output_examples.input: Create a remediation handoff from this redacted credential exposure report.
output: Urgent: The report identifies a credential in a public JavaScript bundle. Rotate it at the provider, then remove it from the build.
Verification: Confirm rotation with the credential owner and check whether older deployments or repository history still contain the credential.

best_practices: Use existing reports for triage and request separate approval for any new network activity.
Keep credential values out of prompts, tickets, and shared reports.
Record skipped checks and review publication settings before any hosted audit.
anti_patterns: Counting skipped checks as passes or treating a clean report as proof of security.
Executing an unverified installer or starting a hosted audit without informed approval.
Removing a leaked credential from source code without rotating it at the provider.

faq.question: Can I review a report without starting a new scan?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide an existing report with sensitive values removed, and ask for analysis without a new audit.

faq.question: What tools produce fresh audit results?
faq.answer: The skill requires the squirrelscan CLI on your system or a connection to the hosted squirrelscan MCP server.

faq.question: Does a passive audit avoid all network requests?
faq.answer: No. A passive audit still crawls pages, but it skips checks that require active probes.

faq.question: Does local execution make an audit passive?
faq.answer: No. Local execution controls where the audit runs. Probe settings control the requests it sends.

faq.question: Can a signed-in audit publish a report?
faq.answer: Yes. Depending on settings, it can use credits and publish an unlisted report. Review those settings before approving a hosted run.

faq.question: What should I do when a credential is exposed?
faq.answer: Rotate it at the provider before removing it from the code. Do not share the credential value.
